To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the neutron capture cross section of 62 Ni at stellar temperatures to be 〈 σ ( kT  ≈ 30 ke V)〉 = 23.3 ± 4.7 mb and the photoactivation cross section of 64 Ni at 13.6 MeV to be σ ( 13.6 M e V) = 2.1 ± 0.4 μ b.
the stellar neutron capture cross sections on 62,63,64 Ni are now known accurately.
we determined the 62 Ni ( γ, γ ) 62 Ni cross section to be 1.3 ± 0.3 mb and the 62 Ni n, γ 63 Ni cross sections to be 23.4  ± 4.5 mb at kT = 25 keV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of neutron and photon cross sections of key isotopes of the s process in the region of A ≈ 60 –90 which are of relevance for the stellar evolution of low mass stars.
the determination of neutron and photon cross sections for key reactions of astrophysics interest, which will allow a better understanding of nucleosynthesis processes in stars.
a systematic study of the 62,63,64 Ni ( n,γ) and 64 Ni (γ,n) reactions, which are important for the s -process nucleosynthesis in low-mass stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 62 Ni ( α, γ ) 66 Zn cross section is still not accurately known, but the 62 Ni problem is solved and the stellar 62 Ni abundance is now well constrained.
our results for the neutron capture cross section of 62 Ni and for the photodisintegration cross section of 64 Ni at low energies are still preliminary and need further confirmation.
the neutron capture cross section of 62 Ni at stellar temperatures is now known to an accuracy of 20%, while the 64 Ni( γ, n ) cross section at 13.3 Me V is known to an accuracy better than 10%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 63 Ni production in the weak s -process has been solved, but the 64 Ni photodissociation is still an open problem.
the 63 Ni production is reduced by more than a factor of 3, which is in agreement with the recent time-of-flight data.
we have measured the neutron capture cross section for 62 Ni at the relevant stellar energies with a precision of better than 20 %.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 62 Ni (n,γ) cross section is significantly smaller than previously assumed, which will have an impact on the stellar 62 Ni abundance and the s-process nucleosynthesis in the A = 90 mass region.
the 63 Ni production in the s process can now be determined accurately, and the stellar 62 Ni problem is finally solved.

the s -process flow is much less sensitive to the 62 Ni (n, γ ) cross section than previously thought, and thus the s -process abundance pattern is not very much affected by a change in this cross section.
